source_text.body:
Write a Forth implementation for the PDP-7
A retired engineer used Claude to write a Forth for the PDP-7 in one morning, including a turtle graphics library and an assembler for the Type 340 display.
·
Nov 24, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
Mitch Bradley, a retired engineer who had written many Forths before (CForth, OpenFirmware), was talked into having Claude write one for the PDP-7. He went to bed skeptical, woke at 7am with ideas, and finished by noon. The result included a turtle graphics library and a Forth-based assembler for Type 340 display instructions.
How it went
It was finished by noon and described as one of the most elegant Forth implementations the commenter had seen. It also runs very fast on a TypeScript PDP-7 emulator with a JavaScript JIT. No test details are given.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I want to write a [language or tool, e.g. Forth interpreter] for [vintage or unusual machine, e.g. PDP-7] in [assembly or host language]. Start by asking me for the instruction set docs or an emulator I have, then build it in small steps, running tests after each one. Finish with a working core plus one demo program like [e.g. turtle graphics], and a short README explaining how to build and run it.
